body:
Hi,

I think the issue here is of the external library. Any reason for using SQLAlchemy-Utils JSONType instead of the builtin one?
As a side note, on postgres you will probably want to use jsonb instead of json as column type

> Hi,
> 
> I think the issue here is of the external library. Any reason for using SQLAlchemy-Utils JSONType instead of the builtin one?
> As a side note, on postgres you will probably want to use jsonb instead of json as column type

main reason for using JSONType is that we run unit tests using in-memory sqlite, and JSON/JSONB does not exist there. JSONType degrades to a text column for platforms like sqlite that don't support JSON directly. It's nicer for unit test purposes to not depend on a database server running externally.

I will look at working around this by not using JSONType and just adding our own type that has hashable=false. And file a ticket against SQLAlchemy-Utils if indeed the bug is there and not here.

> main reason for using JSONType is that we run unit tests using in-memory sqlite, and JSON/JSONB does not exist there. JSONType degrades to a text column for platforms like sqlite that don't support JSON directly

You can use `with_variant` to specify a different type for a particular db.

> It's nicer for unit test purposes to not depend on a database server running externally.

Not sure I agree, since you would then not test on the actual stack that's deployed. But to each its own :)

> I will look at working around this by not using JSONType and just adding our own type that has hashable=false. And file a ticket against SQLAlchemy-Utils if indeed the bug is there and not here.

Ok. Let's also wait for mike's input

I guess I don't understand why the code branch `if self._unique_filter_state` is getting stepped into in the first place. the query is not asking for unique rows only as in `SELECT DISTINCT`. If duplicates are possible then they should be returned seems to me, but this code would exclude dups I think:
```
                    if hashed in uniques:
                        continue
```
In this particular case dups are not possible due to the PK but seems that is beside the point.

I am not an expert in the SQLAlchemy code base however! :)

did your code work in 1.3?   the with_entities() feature had a regression in 1.4 that was fixed in 1.4.19 or thereabouts, which also involved a good deal of new code to make it work the old way.   but functionally it started acting like that of 1.3.x around this version.

> did your code work in 1.3? the with_entities() feature had a regression in 1.4 that was fixed in 1.4.19 or thereabouts, which also involved a good deal of new code to make it work the old way. but functionally it started acting like that of 1.3.x around this version.

Looks like the MCVE does work in 1.3.24:
```
$ pip install SQLAlchemy==1.3.24
Installing collected packages: SQLAlchemy
  Attempting uninstall: SQLAlchemy
    Found existing installation: SQLAlchemy 1.4.18
    Uninstalling SQLAlchemy-1.4.18:
      Successfully uninstalled SQLAlchemy-1.4.18
Successfully installed SQLAlchemy-1.3.24

$ python mcve.py 

this works
13 [1, 2, 3]

this works also
13

this works also. using the JSON type instead of sqlalchemy_utils.JSONType
13 [1, 2, 3]

but this fails with TypeError: unhashable type: list. Problem comes from having AAA.json_column in the with_entities() clause, then iterating over the query:
13 [1, 2, 3]
```

rename.to: has_mapper_entities must update for with_entities calls so that uniqifying is applied appropriately

body:
it's important to note that **sqlalchemy_utils still has a bug here**, their code is wrong.  

however, SQLAlchemy's bug can be illustrated as follows:

```py
from sqlalchemy import Column
from sqlalchemy import create_engine
from sqlalchemy import ForeignKey
from sqlalchemy import Integer
from sqlalchemy import String
from sqlalchemy.ext.declarative import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import declarative_base
from sqlalchemy.orm import relationship
from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

Base = declarative_base()


class A(Base):
    __tablename__ = "a"

    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    data = Column(String)
    bs = relationship("B")


class B(Base):
    __tablename__ = "b"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    a_id = Column(ForeignKey("a.id"))
    data = Column(String)


e = create_engine("sqlite://", echo=True)
Base.metadata.create_all(e)

s = Session(e)

s.add(A(data="a1", bs=[B(data="b1"), B(data="b1"), B(data="b2")]))
s.commit()


r1 = s.query(A.data, B.data).select_from(A).join(B).all()

r2 = s.query(A).select_from(A).join(B).with_entities(A.data, B.data).all()


assert r1 == r2
```

with_entities needs to update the _has_mapper_entities flag.

**Mike Bayer** has proposed a fix for this issue in the **master** branch:

**qualify compile_state updates for non-current entities** https://gerrit.sqlalchemy.org/c/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/+/3016

Thanks for identifying the real issue @zzzeek.

I will file a new one against the the utils lib.

issue.title: JSONType should specify hashable=false

repository.name: sqlalchemy-utils
repository.description: Various utility functions and datatypes for SQLAlchemy.

issue.body:
various JSON things are not hashable. For instance lists and dicts. So the JSONType should let SQLAlchemy know that so it doesn't do things like `if value in some_dict` where value is a JSONType.

To fix this should have a `hashable = False` here:
https://github.com/kvesteri/sqlalchemy-utils/blob/b5b48b13a22aa6d796e98c0225f367a2f010c788/sqlalchemy_utils/types/json.py#L58

This causes certain use cases for JSONType to break in SQLAlchemy 1.4.19 and up. 

For background and a MCVE of the bug, see: https://github.com/sqlalchemy/sqlalchemy/issues/6924
